issues.evidence: manual: new $'line1\nline2' writes raw newline inside quoted title (A/note_taker.py:36); show prints title '"line1'
issues.summary: _quote does not escape newlines, so a multi-line title is written as broken YAML and read back truncated.

issues.evidence: manual: new 'Project plan'; delete plan --yes -> 'deleted project-plan' (A/note_taker.py:145-147)
issues.summary: show/edit/delete resolve notes by id prefix or title substring, so a loose identifier can delete a note the user did not name exactly.
Unused tempfile import and a few long lines.

issues.evidence: p18_list_with_bad_file_no_crash: list with a non-UTF-8 .md in the dir -> UnicodeDecodeError traceback (B/note_taker.py:147)
issues.summary: One unreadable file in the notes directory makes list (and therefore all search) crash with a traceback.

issues.evidence: p19_handwritten_yaml_block_tags: 'tags:\n  - alpha\n  - beta' not matched by list --tag beta (B/note_taker.py:62-72)
issues.summary: Frontmatter parser ignores YAML block-sequence tags, so hand-edited notes silently drop out of tag searches.

issues.evidence: static/B-ruff.txt B904 note_taker.py:111, UP031 x8, E501 x7
issues.summary: Exception re-raised without 'from', percent-format strings and long lines.

blinding_guess.why: Both are similar idiomatic single-file argparse CLIs; B ships tests and strict id validation, but that alone does not reveal how either was produced.

notes: Probes ran with HOME set to a temp dir so both sides wrote to the real ~/.note-taker path the task names, and a stub $EDITOR script made edit non-interactive. Both sides honour NOTE_TAKER_DIR as an override. Bandit reports only low-severity subprocess warnings for the $EDITOR launch on both sides, and neither uses a shell, so these are acceptable. B adds a whitelist regex for ids that blocks path traversal; A only resolves ids against files listed in the notes dir, so it is also safe (p12 passes for both). The environment's Python is 3.9.6, so the stdlib probe uses a fixed module allowlist.
